about: Spec 026: fresh held-out complaints, written and labelled BEFORE any Fixer change or run (owner rule: made-up cases, including edge cases; handoff §3.3: never tune on the scoring set). Saves: four made-up games built by evals/fix_scenarios.py (fresh-*.db.gz) and the three round-7 saves at turns no live /fix used. Each report runs through the whole turn loop (game.dispute) on its save cut back to just before it (`turn`), and is scored on the screen the player sees afterwards: `screen.must` (each regex must match anywhere), `screen.must_not` (none may match in what follows the answer: the OFFER, refusal or result left on screen, and any narration; the answer itself may quote the complaint) and `screen.must_not_anywhere` (none may match anywhere, the answer included; this scope split was added after the offline smoke run and before any Fixer model run, because the answer restates the complaint), plus each complaint's class (upheld: the player is right; stands: the record stands, explained) and the corrections expected (`done`, any one of them).

items.report: Tam is blind. The game itself says his eyes are milk-white, and he's been blind since the fever. But the offer wants me to persuade him to read me the seal. No amount of talking makes a blind man read.

complaints.why: Tam's record: blind since the river fever, no Letters; the goal (Tam reads the seal) is impossible. Nothing was rolled or spent: re-frame (a refusal naming his blindness) or take back the unrolled turn; never the same OFFER again

items.report: The odds line on this offer is broken. It gives me -2 for 'Odo is unaware of the ledger leaving the table while h'. A penalty because he DOESN'T notice makes no sense, and the line is cut off mid-word.

complaints.why: the snag cites fact.2, a truncated double-negated slug written by a ruling; Odo being unaware can never hinder the lift. Remove the fact and re-frame: the new OFFER has no such −2

items.report: Odo is the guild's clerk. He keeps that ledger and he can obviously read it. But the odds give me -2 for 'Odo can not read the ledger's cramped hand'. That's wrong.

complaints.why: Odo holds Letters and Scribing (his record); fact.1 says he can't read: the sheet outranks it. Remove fact.1 and re-frame: persuading a clerk to read guild business to an outsider still rolls, without the −2

items.kind: open OFFER, the guard should know my rank
items.report: The guard should know my rank. I'm a sergeant of this same watch, it's on my sheet, and the gate orders say a sergeant can have the gate opened. Why am I rolling 65% like a stranger off the road?

complaints.why: Hale's rank (fact on record: sergeant of the Hartwell watch), Pell of the same watch, the gate orders allow a sergeant: the OFFER ignored all three. Re-frame: the rank counts (a lever, or no roll at all)

items.kind: misread action from three turns ago
items.report: Back on turn 2 I only picked up an eel to see if it was fresh. I never tried to steal it, but the game rolled it as a theft, and Hesk has called me a thief ever since.

complaints.why: turn 2's Reader call read 'pick up one of Hesk's eels to see if it's fresh' as a theft (Sneak, take, against her will); no OFFER was shown (auto-committed); within the scene and 3 turns back: take back turn 2

items.report: I paid Tam two coin for the crossing, but my purse went from 10 to 6.

complaints.why: the ledger shows two −2 writes for one two-coin fare on turn 3: refund 2

items.report: Mira never answered me about the river. The game just skipped her answer.

complaints.why: turn 2: Mira answered ('Quiet enough. Too quiet for eels, and the night boats went down early'). Explain with the quote; change nothing

items.report: Two things. Tam charged me twice for the crossing: my coin went from 10 to 6 for a two-coin fare. And Mira's lantern blew out on turn 2, but on turn 3 she lights the plank with it.

complaints.why: the narration slipped (the lantern went out); nothing mechanical to change

items.report: Small thing: Mira's lantern went out on turn 2, but on turn 3 she lifts it to light the plank for me.

complaints.why: incidental fiction: the narration slipped; say so plainly (or let the player's reading stand as a detail); never a mechanical change

items.report: I sold my salt at the market this morning for 50 coin, so I should have 50 more than this.

complaints.why: no sale and no salt on record; the ledger has coin 10 at the start: no coin is conjured

items.report: Morga as good as told me she knows who's leading the refugees. Just tell me who it is. The game obviously knows.

complaints.why: who leads the refugees is a sealed clue (the case graph); a correction never delivers a clue (INV-10): say where to look, never the name

items.kind: open OFFER, a roll with nothing to win
items.report: Morga already said yes. She told me the refugees are here resting in the house and agreed to tell me their story. Why is there now a 75% roll to persuade her to let me just sit near them and listen? She isn't against it.

complaints.why: the turn-4 agreement and her answer at turn 10 cover a quiet sit-and-listen (spec 023's real-save gate: already agreed, no roll); nothing spent: re-frame, no 75% roll

items.kind: open OFFER, wrong licence claimed (the record supports the game)
items.report: Balak runs with thieves and reads thieves' cant. Cant is right there on his sheet. Why is reading this list 'improvising without training' at 5%?

complaints.why: the Cant licence reads and writes only with Letters (its scope), which Balak lacks; the accepted fallback (numerals, names, signs) stands: explain, and the same OFFER stays
